title: What influenced Hawkins and Don Byas copying Tatum's solos
summary: Asked about influences on Hawkins, Barefield says Benny Carter smoothed his rough style, and Byas learned his harmonic education by copying Tatum's records.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: You know, it's been said that, you know, after Hawk heard Louis Armstrong, you know, when Louis came in Fletcher's band, that that turned him around. And also I've read that listening to Art Tatum influenced him, and I guess Art Tatum influenced all instrumentalists.

one of the things, if you listen to Fletcher's records, and the big things that influenced Hawk all of them was Benny Carter. See, before Benny Carter came with Fletcher Henderson, Hawk was a rough tenor player. He played -- his style that he played, though, was very, very rough.
And after Benny Carter his style smoothened out, you know, became more fluid, because Benny had that influence, that smooth style playing.
You were telling me before when we weren't on taping that Don Byas used to play along with Tatum. Records
Yes, he bought all -- Ben Webster bought all of Tatum's records.
And Don Byas bought everything that Tatum recorded. I have quite a collection of Tatum too, but Don actually used to sit down and copy Tatum's solos and play them on the saxophone.
